In a source-matched all-Naval-No Roman Empire versus Britons test, Rome publishes scaled capability 8820 (88.20/100) and selects COMPETITIVE while Britons publish 6287 (62.87/100) and select SUPPORT; Rome may maintain the larger fleet despite Naval No on both sides.

In a source-matched Naval Yes plus Naval No team test, the Yes ally selects PRIMARY, the No ally selects SUPPORT, the support ally never launches an independent naval attack, and its completed-plus-queued combat fleet remains at its three-percent cap unless the audited heavy-hull exception raises it to five percent.

In a source-matched all-Naval-No team test, only the highest-scoring allied AI selects COMPETITIVE unless capability ties; a lower-scoring ally yields after reading the published allied capability goal.
An eligible support civilization produces no more than two Quadrireme/Quinquereme-line hulls and one Octeres while retaining Scout, Fire, Boarding, and Juggernaut escort/bombardment coverage.
known_limits: The engine exposes map-zone and observed resource counts, not terrain area; twelve resources are a documented settlement proxy and must be calibrated in fresh replays.
A remote Town Center does not redefine position-self. Home-centered economy systems remain anchored to the original town, while the new defense and housing paths explicitly use the colony point.

The colony-established and colony-Town-Center sentinels are not yet cleared automatically if every settler dies, the colony is exhausted, or its Town Center is destroyed; per-zone lifecycle remains unresolved.
Asset scans use bounded DUC search lists. A very large economy can still hide an attacked villager beyond a role list, although attacked economic buildings are searched separately.

For shoreline land attackers, distance from the attacked asset is only a coastal-reachability proxy; the engine exposes no general warship-to-land-target path query, so a disconnected nearby basin remains a fresh-replay risk.

Exact target commands prevent target drift but do not mathematically enforce a maximum-range annulus; pathing, obstruction handling, weapon-form state, distance discipline, and runtime command ownership still require replay evidence.

The siege controllers currently inspect the closest enemy player. Their exact-target behavior is therefore calibrated for the present one-versus-one test and requires enemy iteration before it is reliable in free-for-all matches.
Pummel is not an identifier in the current DAT, strings, unit lines, or AI constants. The implemented land controller assumes the user meant the Battering Ram, Capped Ram, and Siege Ram family.
The replay cannot identify whether clustered unknown DELETE commands removed a Town Center foundation; cancellation telemetry and a source-matched replay are still required.
The inspected MainLog is not a usable whole-match oracle because most of it is repetitive UnitAIModule trace output.

Structural and synchronization validators cannot prove up-allied-goal timing, role convergence with human allies, Shipyard placement success, or whether global attack-now respects every reserved specialist group; the three naval matchup acceptance cases require fresh runtime evidence.

The global food-gathering reach remains unchanged because it also governs forage access. Structural checks cannot prove whether engine autotasking still assigns too many villagers to distant shore fish; P3B8 telemetry and a fresh replay must determine whether a distance-specific fisherman retask or hard cap is also required.

Farm telemetry reports completed farms but not pending foundations, available wood, or placement feasibility. It can expose target suppression and lack of completed growth, but command-stream and resource evidence are still required to distinguish insufficient wood, accepted pending placement, rejected placement, and rule ownership failures.

The competitive score now captures steady-state hull quality including projectile/blast-area lethality, population-discounted garrison firepower for Tessarakonteres, cost/population efficiency, audited and forced line upgrades, support-upgrade access, missing Conscription, Shipyard work rate, and ship train time. Carthaginian Cothon batch cost and throughput are validated and retained as potential evidence but excluded from the runtime score because the AI does not yet construct and operate Cothon batches. Research discounts, free-upgrade timing, and age-of-unlock readiness remain explicit unscored calibration inputs because the current evaluator cannot yet derive them consistently across every mutually exclusive DAT technology branch.

direct_replay_observations: The replay parsed without errors and ended normally at 110:44 when the Roman Empire resigned; Rome reached Early, Middle, and Imperial at 11:13, 21:08, and 45:22, while Britons reached them at 12:03, 21:30, and 38:27.

None of 2967 decoded chat records contains the expected RAWAI-P3B8 marker or its farm telemetry, so the complete deployed build cannot be attributed to repository HEAD 41e6164 even though some migration telemetry fingerprints match.

Migration scout attempts fired at 11:37, 14:37, and 17:38. The first Roman Transport Ship MAKE request was not issued until 14:21, and no migration transport, boarding, departure, landing, or failure telemetry followed any attempt.
At 21:09 through 23:11, five gate snapshots each reported two Transport Ships, idle-villager bucket zero, home defense zero, global depletion zero, and utility-controller sum zero.
Transport objects 11576 and 11607 received no post-creation orders until roughly 69 minutes, leaving each inactive for about 51 to 54 minutes despite the migration gate seeing both by 21:09.

Transport 11607 later received repeated boarding, movement, and unload commands from 69:14 through 79:53, including large destination reversals and shoreline ping-pong. Replay telemetry nevertheless reported zero loaded transports every approximately 20 seconds from 43:42 through 110:35.

A 48-unit Roman group was retasked six times in twelve seconds around nearly identical assembly coordinates at 75:08 through 75:20; twenty of those units then received boarding orders toward transport 11607.

Four completed, villager-producing Roman Town Centers were explicitly deleted at 95:11 through 95:24. Current source has no autonomous completed-Town-Center deletion rule, making manual or external intervention the strongest attribution, although the replay records only player ownership.

Fourteen Roman naval dispatch telemetry events occurred from 50:28 through 105:57, Roman warboat count reached sixteen, and total warboat losses reached eighteen. This falsifies a claim that the navy never dispatched, but does not establish useful target acquisition or movement before the first group waypoint at 48:42.
implementation_inferences: The civilian migration gate depended on engine-idle villagers or whole-known-map depletion, so assigned fishermen on a mine-depleted starting island could leave both conditions false even while two idle utility transports existed.

Scout opportunities were consumed before a hull was selected; three early landing-search failures could therefore permanently exhaust the bounded scouting system before transport production became usable.

Migration sent loaded ships directly toward an inland natural-resource point and bypassed the military transport screen, tower scan, corridor waypoint, and recall controller. A disconnected basin, unreachable beach, or known defended direct corridor could therefore stall or destroy the mission.

The migration hull was stored only by ID and not reserved in a direct-control group, while global attack-now remained free to retask transport assembly. This left command ownership vulnerable to the observed boarding and movement churn.

Attack timer ownership was cleared when a transient eligibility gate failed, after which the timer module restarted a full interval. This could add long passive gaps rather than a short readiness retry.

The shared position-self point was continuously rewritten from an arbitrary current Town Center, and a Juggernaut evasion rule explicitly moved warships to that inland point. Land and water controllers therefore did not have stable domain-specific anchors.

Defense suppression was enabled before local or naval response rules established that any same-zone responder existed, allowing an unreachable remote attack to suppress offense without producing a useful defense group.
changes_under_test: Emit RAWAI-P3B11 and require an exact deployment-manifest match before attributing subsequent replay behavior to this patch.

Every 45 seconds in Middle Antiquity or later, count observed Gaia gold and stone only on the immutable starting-Town-Center land zone and publish a separate home-mine-pressure signal without conflating it with whole-map depletion.

Give civilian relocation priority when starting-land mines are exhausted, require a real Transport Ship before either migration mission starts, include assigned noncritical fishermen in evacuation, and consume a scout attempt only after a hull is selected and reserved.

Reserve the selected migration hull in its own direct-control group, capture its water-valid origin, return empty ships to that origin instead of an inland Town Center, and release ownership on every idle terminal path.

Keep landed settlers and the migration hull reserved until the matching Mining Camp, Lumber Camp, or Mill foundation is found in the destination land zone, explicitly assign those settlers to its exact object ID, and publish the colony only after that foundation completes; if placement or construction fails, reboard the same settlers for a bounded return and direct any carried resources to a home Town Center.

Before departure, sample both lateral mid-route corridors for known Towers, Sea Towers, Castles, and Town Centers; hold the mission when both are defended, repeatedly drive the hull through the selected bounded waypoint, and recall it after four measured no-progress checks rather than four checks during a long but advancing voyage.
Bound an aborted ferry to four origin-unload retries plus one final watchdog window, and centrally release both the transport and passenger reservation groups on every idle terminal path.

Permit emergency Transport Ship production at the authoritative 125-wood DAT cost after starting-land mine depletion instead of requiring the normal 35-wood production buffer, and demand at least two hulls there so one busy transport cannot suppress its replacement.

On true island maps, defer land attack-now until completed Transport Ships cover a full army lift plus utility hull and every direct transport controller is idle; queued hulls no longer satisfy readiness.
Prioritize a confirmed remote colony Town Center under home-mine pressure and suppress ordinary additional starting-island Town Centers while preserving a zero-Town-Center last-resort recovery rule.
Keep position-self fixed at its startup land anchor and send a ranged warship evading a nearby Juggernaut toward the nearest own Port or Shipyard rather than a Town Center.

Defer global land and naval attack dispatch while migration or transport routing owns a hull, restrict the combined periodic attack to land maps, and retry transiently blocked attack timers after twenty seconds instead of a full interval.

Count eligible same-zone land and naval responders before aborting attacks and setting global home defense, and record a bounded no-responder diagnostic instead of freezing offense around an empty response group.
fresh_replay_acceptance: The deployment checker reports identical runtime manifests and replay chat contains RAWAI-P3B11 near match start.

No scout attempt is recorded before at least one completed empty Transport Ship exists; after a hull is selected, telemetry records its ID, a boarding target, loaded count, route-side decision, waypoint progress, and either a landed scout or an explicit abort reason.

When both known starting-land mine classes reach zero while remote naturals are known, home-mine pressure becomes one and civilian migration starts even if at least two waiting villagers remain classified as fishermen rather than engine-idle.

A selected migration transport receives no departure command before its recorded garrison count meets the one-scout target or the two-settler partial minimum, retains stable ownership during boarding, and does not repeat the 69 to 80 minute board-move-unload churn.

The migration route uses one selected lateral waypoint, retries no more than four times if it makes no progress, refuses two known defended corridors, unloads on the intended resource-bearing land zone, and returns the empty hull toward its captured water origin.

A moving transport on a long route resets its stall counter when distance to the waypoint falls; an unreachable return performs no more than four origin unload retries and one final watchdog attempt before releasing transport ownership.
An island land attack does not dispatch while its completed transport count is below the full-lift target or migration, route, recovery, relic, repair, or harbor-clearing owns the transport channel.

After a starting island loses its mines, transported settlers remain reserved, receive an explicit build order on a matching correct-zone resource drop-off, and publish the colony only after that drop-off completes; a failed drop-off attempt reboards available settlers, unloads them at the captured home shore, and targets a home Town Center so carried resources can be deposited.

A transient attack-readiness failure produces another eligibility check after about twenty seconds, while active migration or route ownership does not produce repeated inland transport assembly orders.

A remote attacked asset with zero same-zone responders emits the no-responder diagnostic and does not globally latch home defense; a reachable threat reports a positive responder count before offense is aborted.
A ranged warship evading a nearby Juggernaut moves toward a Port or Shipyard shoreline anchor, and establishing or deleting a remote Town Center does not change the replay-visible startup home point.
known_limits: The replay command stream does not expose actual transport occupancy, reached positions, path splines, fog-of-war knowledge at decision time, individual death causes, or whether ordinary movement and construction orders were manual.

The engine exposes no arbitrary ship-to-beach path query. The new migration waypoint has a progress watchdog and water-valid origin but still requires a fresh replay to prove the selected bounded point is navigable.
Migration route defense scans currently inspect the selected target player and sampled midpoint regions, not every segment or every hostile owner in a team or free-for-all match.
A known-safe sampled corridor is not a proof against defenses hidden in fog. Unlike the military route controller, a one-unit scout ferry cannot use its own land scout as an advance naval screen.

A reservation group and repeated direct movement order do not structurally prove that the engine attack manager can never overwrite a transport; runtime command ownership remains a replay acceptance item.

Remote drop-offs are the primary island logistics path; the return ferry is a bounded recovery path for a failed colony establishment, not an inefficient per-resource-load shuttle. Foundation ownership, completion, reboarding, and final cargo deposit still require fresh replay confirmation.

Starting-land pressure counts observed mine objects, not remaining resource amount or terrain area. An unexplored home mine can cause a false-positive signal, while a visible but nearly exhausted mine delays it until the object disappears.

The replay shows fourteen naval dispatches and a sixteen-warboat fleet, so remaining naval usefulness is a target, zone, and command-ownership problem rather than an absence-of-production problem; direct main-fleet rally replacement remains unresolved.

For a coastal land attacker the AI can command nearby naval support but still cannot prove water-path compatibility. That branch no longer globally retreats the army or latches home defense, and its actual support value requires fresh replay evidence.

The completed Town Center deletes are strongly inferred as manual or external because current source lacks that action, but the replay does not identify the human or AI command issuer separately from player ownership.
